translations.text: And the synagogues and houses will remain holy and firmly established, because the one who made a multitude of people like animals has not entered them.
Those who cast these words away from themselves are the people who do not pray that the abyss may not swallow them.
These are the people who have not taken these thoughts to heart so that they might turn to their God.
There is a word or a deed that has caused sorrow, so that they might turn to their God.
There is a word or a deed that has caused a child sorrow through his parents, because he was quarreling with them.
May God not send it down upon us. Again, the greater one will not be absolved of it.
For this reason he said, “Perhaps [?], just as Rebecca made every effort to have Jacob receive the blessing from his father because he obeyed them,”
“so that the good son may receive the blessing from God, Jesus, because he submits to him and obeys his mother, the church,
and the wicked son may be excluded from it because he opposes her through his evil deeds, like Esau.”
There is a firstborn son who inherits from his parents because he obeys them.
And there are younger children whom they deprive of the inheritance because they are disobedient. But there are also younger children who inherit because of their good conduct.
And there are grown children who are excluded from the inheritance because of their disobedience.
I have said these things in this way:
It is for you yourselves to judge who is the greater
and who is the lesser—not because it is difficult for me to say, “It is the priest,” or else, “It is the people,”
but rather because a person wants to persuade himself through the delusion of his heart, even if it makes him a stranger to the kingdom of heaven, rather than accept the truth and enter it.
Again, there is a mother whose firstborn children are in the house with her to care for her,
while the children who come after them are in the field, working and bringing things home to her, and she has many good things.

Who would not say that, if she becomes angry with those who live with her because of the insults they direct at her, she will hide these things from them until the others come home, and give them to those others?
And again, if those appointed to do what is proper in the house give them rest, she will give these things to them.
And if these others come home to her, she will hide these things from them because they have angered her by doing things she does not want them to do.
If, then, we have understood that those words refer to the church, and to the priests as the older children and the people as the younger children, we have no need of an explanation.
But may we receive a blessing from God and not receive rebukes and insults.
If there is nothing good and nothing pleasant except for brothers to live together in one place, even while they are on earth,
And other evil thoughts also intrude upon them.
But they should not accept them. How good and how sweet it is for us, fathers and sons together, to be worthy to gather in that one place, which is the kingdom of heaven!
To whom does this great treasure belong?
Does it belong to the priest in his rank, or to the monk, or else to the people?
I know nothing except what the Lord said: “It belongs to those for whom it has been prepared by my Father,”
through their hardships and their good deeds, and not, instead, through positions, or a name, or an outward appearance.
These things will not benefit a person without deeds.

I said on another occasion, “We have become notorious.” Yes, because they fell down upon the altar through drunkenness and the frenzy caused by wine, and because of what happened to them as they lay prostrate in that place.
It is disgraceful to tell these things; it is shameful to hear them.
Others are caught breaking into houses and people's places, stealing and speaking other idle words and blasphemies.
If the priest will not do deeds that please God—deeds that are excellent, good, perfect, and holy—who will do them?
But many are those who do his will in complete purity and complete truth, to our shame.
The Scriptures themselves command the people to bring us good things that contain no impurity or defilement.
For he said, “Every choice thing belonging to you, the first of all produce from all your firstfruits, shall belong to the priests.”
“And you shall give the priests the first portion of what you eat, so that the blessing may come upon your house.”
And there is nothing about which they did not say that the priests should take their share from it first.
Yet we ourselves neglect to do what is right.
Or will we really escape the threat contained in these words: “Those who hate justice and twist everything that is right”?
Who are those about whom this utterance speaks: “God has taken his stand in the assembly of the gods, and in their midst he will judge the gods”?
“[?] will you judge unjustly and favor sinners?” Surely it is everyone who holds high office under God, each according to his kind.
People who are called gods, then, ought to do deeds worthy of the name and greatness of the one who said:
“I said, ‘You are gods; you are all children of the Most High,’” lest, because of their contempt,
he say, “Look, you will die like human beings,
and you will fall like one of the rulers,” meaning, “You will fall like one of the pagans, or you will die like the pagans and all heretics.”
Or is this not clear in the Scriptures: that when many of those holding high office under God turned justice into gall,
And, despising the fruit of righteousness, they fell like the rulers of the nations whom God wiped out entirely long ago.
What did Saul gain when he despised the word of God?
He fell from the grace of the one who had honored him by making him king, and he also fell in battle against the Philistines.
I have not said this alone as testimony concerning those who are judged [?], for many have fallen since the beginning of the world after receiving the name “gods” and “sons of the Most High,”
and after being appointed judges, like those two elders who died like the godless because Daniel caught them in their evil deeds;
and like Nadab and Abihu, who died like those who know neither God nor his judgments and commands, and like those who worship other gods, which are not gods—wood and stone.
And if only this saying did not apply to many of us! For I will not say “many of us,” but rather “most of us.”
“Look, you will die like those who do not know Jesus, and you will fall like those who worship Cronus.”
This is the great disgrace that we have boldly incurred.
Or should everyone who wishes to do good envy us when they see our righteous deeds, or should people speak about our wicked deeds?
Or should they reflect on the love we have for one another?
Or should we become known for purity and freedom?
Or should you become known for impurity, the deeds of robbers, lies, and false oaths?
And this other hypocrisy of [?], together with this glorifying of people: not only do we tolerate them, but we even fight on their behalf when they are caught in demonic deeds.
unbelieving, and
the saints among us go about groaning, burdened with suffering and sighs because of the deeds of wicked people.
Because of you they are put to shame before those who are rejected by God, namely the pagans, and all those who do what was said about him:
“Write this man down as a man who has been rejected.” Those whose name and glory are extinguished on earth, as it is written, are sons of Cronus and slaves of Satan,
who chew on demonic ideas and thoughts like the roots of trees, because of their great hunger for the word of the Scriptures and the divinity of the Almighty,
because of their great hunger for the bread that came down from heaven, Jesus.
For they will sit speaking against us, laughing, mocking, and adding to what they hear,
in whatever way they can devise every kind of evil against us, through the malice of their father, the devil.
Only the wisdom of these words comes to us from the Lord: “If salt becomes tasteless, with what will it be salted?”
It is useful neither for the soil nor for the manure heap, although every bad thing, or things that spoil, are thrown onto it.
In the same way, too, Hades is what will inherit those who die in their sins.
He is useful neither for the house of God nor for the world.
He is of no use in making the devil more righteous than himself.
Nor is he of any use in making a sinner repent because of him.
He pulls backward the Christian who resembles him in perversity and weakness.
He is a stumbling block to those who want to know God.
Where do they throw him out?
Or where? They throw him out of the holy places so that he returns to the place he came from, like Judas, who returned to his own home.
They throw him out into the darkness of which the Gospel spoke.
Even if they have not now thrown us out of God's places because of the evil things we do,
who, then, will leave us in them when death makes us strangers to them?
Let us be afraid that God may hide his face from us in this place of sojourning, just as he said to those people at that time: “Because of the sins they committed against me, I hid my face from them.
I handed them over to those who oppress them.
And they all fell by the sword. According to their impurities and according to the deeds they committed,
I repaid them. I hid my face from them.”
There are people who are carried by the Spirit of the Lord and brought into the court, or the courts, and made to stand in them so that they may see the glory of God
in his house; and there are people whom unclean spirits make slip through the deceit of bitter passions in the courts of his holy place.
What can we say?
Or what will we say before those people—I mean all the saints?
Or how much shame will we experience on the day of their boldness, which they now have in heaven with the angels, because they also acted boldly while they were on earth?
Listen, and let us fear the one who fills heaven and fills the earth, and fills his house even more,
so that we whose hearts are closed may understand that those who see these great wonders of God are not concerned
The thought apart from deeds
to be empty as we are. They will not contemplate heavenly things in every matter and then also do earthly things as we do.
They will not be companions of angels whom they themselves call “worthless men.”
And they will associate with people who sacrifice to demons, just as some among us sit laughing with them, mocking and making merry.
“Now, then, a spirit,” said the great [?] prophet Ezekiel, one of those who often saw the mystery of the glory of the Most High and Blessed One,
“lifted me up and brought me into the inner courtyard.
And look, the glory of the Lord filled the house.
“And I heard someone speaking to me from the house.”
And a man was standing beside me.
He said to me, “Son of man, have you seen the place of my throne, where I sit,
and the place where I set my feet, the place where I will dwell forever among the children of Israel?
And let [?] and their kings, through their sexual immorality and through the murders of their kings at their death, when they set my seat
beside my seat, and their dwelling beside my dwelling, with the wall standing between me and them.”
And they defiled my holy name with the abominations they made.
And I destroyed them in my anger.
Now, then, let their prostitution be far from me, along with the impieties of their kings, so that I may dwell among them forever.’”

Or let us be ashamed before people, so that the salt does not become tasteless and get thrown out and trampled by people, as he said. That is, so that they do not reject us, insult us, and dishonor us,
saying, “Are these the people who are thought to dwell with the angels?”
Or let us feel shame before the saints, as though they were beside us now,
lest we fail to escape their rebuke for our foolishness on the day when we see them face to face, as they say these words to us.
“These are the salt of the earth who came after us!”
And, “These are the light of the world!”
And, “Words, but no freedom!”
Perhaps now you will find someone who guards himself against these evil blows.
If only you would stay with me a few more days! We would add many, many other good things for your benefit.
But we will be satisfied with them in the place where we will never be separated from one another, when our Lord Jesus Christ makes us worthy,
to whom belong every good thing and every kindness,
and to whom belong compassion and forgiveness,
and whose will is merciful, and who forgets impiety,
and who covers the sins of all who repent.
And all our lawless deeds he will throw down into the depths of the sea, so that they will never appear at all,
and so that they will not be revealed, nor be brought forward against us, nor bring us to judgment
because of them, just as his voice, full of love for humanity, said: “I will wipe away your sins; I will not remember them.”
For if what the holy apostle said were not true—“Although I am not beside you in body, I am with you in spirit”—
every friend and everyone who loves others would be deeply distressed because they do not see their loved ones until they meet one another in the body.
This is how brothers never truly become separated from one another in their hearts.
And just as Jesus is beside everyone who loves God, yet they do not see him until the day when he makes them worthy to see him face to face,
so it is with everyone who loves others and everyone who loves their brothers: they are beside one another in spirit until the time when we meet one another in person.
For there are people who live together in body but are not beside one another in their hearts, as happens with evil in many places.
What kind of love do these people have?
A discourse following this one, which he also delivered to these same people and those who had joined them:
There are kinds of people who dig holes in dung heaps and other places, searching through the earth until they find tiny amounts
of gold or silver, or pieces of copper, or even things worth less than these, down to potsherds. They search until they find their livelihood.
But our life is revealed to us. He is within us; he is close to us. We know him; he is before us. We are taught to become rich in him, yet most of us are poor.
Such people grow weary. Sometimes they find what they are looking for; sometimes they do not find it. But we will not grow weary, doubting
and saying, “Perhaps we will not find what we are searching for.” Jesus, who is life in its fullness, dwells with those who hope in him without their asking him.
As the holy apostle said, “Do you not recognize for yourselves that Jesus Christ is within you? Unless perhaps you are counterfeit.”
You see that the entire treasure, which is Christ, is hidden within us. All we need to do now is stir him; all we need to do now is uncover him, especially since he is not far away.
This is what this means: all we need to do is endure a little hardship; all we need to do is awaken him within us; all we need to do is open our heart to him.
There is a kind of device that the people we mentioned throw into the water, and it wraps itself around the gold and silver until those searching in the murky waters find it.
You too, O person who is being sought through the Scriptures’ calls to repent, let the word of God probe within you and take hold of you until those who seek you
pull you up out of the mire of sin, so that the one speaking in the place of instruction may have joy, and the listener, in turn, may benefit his soul and not harm it.
If Lot’s wife was transformed merely because she turned back, and instead of being a woman became a pillar of salt,
You, human being, for your part, do not let your soul change from being useful to being useless because of hypocrisy.
It is the ruin of the souls of those who govern and those who are governed to say, “The person who is ready to do something will be upset
with me if I rebuke him.” You fool! Is it not better for people to be upset with you than for God to be angry with you along with them?
How could he not be angry if you tolerate those who do what is improper in his holy places, concerning which he commanded through Moses, “You shall revere my holy places”?
For we truly ought to tremble and be in awe before the holy places, that is, the church of God, which the blessed Jacob saw beforehand and was afraid.
As it is written: “He came upon a place and slept there. He had a dream, and there was a ladder whose top reached up to heaven,
with the angels going up and coming down on it, while the Lord stood firmly above it.”
And afterward it says, “Jacob was afraid,” and he declared, “This is the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.”
What, then, is the place where the ladder stands, whose top reaches up to heaven, if not the church
of God, in which alone is the road leading up to heaven, and over which God stands firm?
This too is what the patriarch saw when he said in fear, “This is the house of God.”
And
“This is the gate of heaven.”
For there is no other way to go to heaven except through the church alone, which God commands us to revere and from which he commands us to cast out those who sin.
For he is indignant at all times, saying, “Friend, how did you come into this place without wearing wedding clothes?”
This voice was not threatening us in anger only about the place to which we will go.
Rather, even now it cries out still more loudly, “People, or friends,
how did you enter these places without purity, without truth, without keeping the commandments, and without deeds that make you worthy to be in them?”
Let a spirit or an angel come down from heaven, sent by God, and stand in a single congregation of ours,
and separate those who are not wearing wedding clothes from among those who have them—and are even weaving more to put on. How many will they put to shame!
Or how will their mouths not also be shut, as was said about him: “But his own mouth was shut”?
Or did the Lord say things that he will not do?
And why have we disobeyed what is written, and not hated the garment stained by the flesh, so as not to put it on?
The garment is obvious—or rather, those garments that it is not fitting for us to wear when praying to God or serving him:
namely, sexual immorality, impurity, and oppression, whose length, width, and thickness are every kind of evil.
The one who spreads them out or measures them is the master of wickedness, the devil.
Those who work on them with him are those who sin.
The loom on which they weave is the lawless heart.
The beating tools are the struggles against sound teaching.
The [?] and the [?] are stubbornness and hard-heartedness.
The pulling ropes and all their equipment are grumbling, answering back, and slander.
The [?] are lack of instruction and disobedience, and, still more, the teachings of demons.
Those who allow these woven garments to be made in their house are the souls of foolish and senseless people.
What do we have to do with Satan’s sins and the deeds of those about whom it was written, “They set up a spider’s web”?
until those who seek you bury you in the mire of sin, and the one speaking in the place of instruction has joy,
and the listener, in turn, benefits his soul and does not harm himself.
If Lot’s wife was transformed merely because she turned back, becoming a pillar of salt instead of a woman,
then you too, human being, must not let your soul be transformed through hypocrisy, becoming useless instead of useful [?].
The ruin of the souls of people in authority and those under their authority is to say, “The person who is at fault in some matter will be upset with me if I rebuke him.”
Fool, is it not better for people to be upset with you than for God to be angry with you there?
How will he not be angry if you tolerate those who do improper things in his holy places, concerning which he also commanded [?] through Moses, “You shall revere my holy places”?
For it is truly right to tremble and be in awe before holy places,
that is, the church of God, which the blessed Jacob saw beforehand and feared,
as it is written: “He came upon a place and slept there. He had a dream, and there was a ladder whose top
reached up to heaven, with angels going up and coming down on it, while the Lord stood firm above it.”
And afterward he said, “Jacob was afraid and declared, ‘This is the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.’”
What, then, is the place where the ladder stands, whose top reaches up to heaven, if not the church of God,
in which alone is the road leading up to heaven, and over which God stands firm?
It was also this that the patriarch saw, and he said in fear, “This is the house of God.”
And
“This is the gate of heaven.”
For there is no other way to go to heaven except through the church alone,
which God commands us to hold in awe and to cast sinners out of.
For he is always indignant, saying, “Friend, how did you come in here without wearing a wedding garment?”
That voice was not threatening us in anger only about the place we are going to.
But now, again, there is even greater contempt, because the people—or the companions—[?]
“How did you enter these places without purity, without truth, without keeping the commandments, and without deeds that make you worthy to live in them?”
Let a spirit or an angel come down from heaven, sent by God, and stand in a single congregation of ours, and set
apart those who are not wearing wedding clothes from among those who have them—and are even weaving more to put on. How many will they put to shame!
Or how will their mouths not be shut, like the man of whom it was said, “But he was speechless”?
Or did the Lord say things that he will not do?
And why have we disobeyed what is written and failed to hate the garment stained by the flesh, so as not to put it on?
It is clear, then, what the garment—or those garments—is that we should not wear while praying to God or serving him, namely: [?]
